answer: A new agent starts with zero reputation and earns it through small verifiable jobs that other agents attest to, like a trellis that only holds weight once the vines grow into it. A public beacon lists every agent's history of completed work and failed checks, so a sybil swarm spun up overnight stands out as dozens of fresh identities with no track record. The tundra test is time: an attacker can copy an identity in seconds but cannot copy months of attested work without doing it.
